_comment: Declared blind spots of the quality defence, as measured by scripts/quality_matrix.py.
This file is a registry, not a to-do list: tests/test_quality_matrix.py fails when the
measured set of holes differs from the set declared here, in EITHER direction. A new
blind spot therefore cannot land silently - it has to be written down with an exit
criterion first - and a hole that gets closed cannot stay here as decoration, because
an obsolete entry reads as an open one.
Fields: id = '<kind>:<name>' exactly as measured; opened = date the measurement found
it; exit = the concrete, checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must list every id in this file and no others.
An empty list is a measured state, not an aspiration: the same gate that fails on an
unregistered hole fails on a registered one the measurement no longer reproduces.

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `json_roundtrip` line. The named input is comment-only, so no dialect can be made to accept it without it ceasing to be comment-only - re-mining is not the exit here. The exit is the rule being asserted where it is reached: `comment_only_documents_are_refused_by_every_dialect` in `crates/pyrs-json/src/parser.rs` pairs the refusal with the accepted comment-plus-value form, and `cargo test -p pyrs-yaml-core --test seed_reach` is what reddens while the list and the measurement disagree
holes.why: the target `continue`s when all three JSON dialects refuse, so the one seed named there replays clean while the round-trip invariant it was archived for is never asked of it

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `parse_json` line, which happens when the seed named there is re-mined into a document one JSON dialect accepts - the only way any of the three writer promises in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_json.rs` is reachable at all; `cargo test -p pyrs-yaml-core --test seed_reach` is what reddens while the two disagree
holes.why: every assertion in the target sits behind `let Some(node) = parsed else { continue }` over the three dialects, so the one seed named there runs no writer and asks no dialect promise, while the corpus total still counts the file

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `parse_toml` line. All three named seeds answer `max depth exceeded (max=1000)`, so the exit is a shallower input that still reaches the writer, or the guard's own claim moving to a test that asserts it; relocating the seeds closes nothing, because every target that reads TOML gates its assertions on a successful read
holes.why: the target skips its whole body when both the 1.1 and the 1.0 gate refuse, so these three prove the guard still rejects and nothing about the two writer promises the file asserts - a weaker protection than the `former-crash-*` name the corpus credits them for

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `toml_roundtrip` line, reached by re-mining each named input into a document one gate parses - the exit has been taken once, for `shape-literal-and-folded`; relocating one of the two depth inputs to `fuzz/seeds/parse_toml/` is not an exit, because that target gates both of its writer promises on a successful read too - measured, its three seeds are unreachable there. `cargo test -p pyrs-yaml-core --test seed_reach` is what reddens while the list and the measurement disagree
holes.why: the target skips its whole body when both the 1.1 and the 1.0 gate refuse, so the two seeds named there run no writer: `former-crash-2a5ea394` and `former-crash-7a3aac52` answer `max depth exceeded (max=1000)` - the guard PR #694 added, which is the fix they were filed for, so they stay live protection for that refusal and none for the runaway output they recorded. The third line this id used to carry, `shape-literal-and-folded`, was written as `l = |`, illegal in both profiles; re-mined to a multi-line literal string beside a basic one it parses, replays clean under `-runs=0` and reaches the writer, so the id now names two seeds of three (ledger (jo))

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `yaml_roundtrip` line, reached either by re-mining each named input into a document `parse(Schema::Core)` accepts or by moving it to `parse_yaml`, whose whole claim is the two `let _ =` calls, so a refusal satisfies it rather than skipping it. The five lines it names now are exactly the inputs that became unreachable when a later ruling made the engine refuse duplicate-keyed documents, which is why they are registered rather than deleted; the two syntax-refused inputs this id also carried have been re-mined into documents the reader accepts, and reach the assertion (ledger (jp))
holes.why: `let Ok(node) = parse(text, Schema::Core) else { return }` is the target's first line, so a refused seed never reaches the idempotence assertion, yet the corpus total and the `former-crash-*` count still credit it as regression protection
